messages.author: 7f93d72765248a41
messages.subject: Minimum sample size
parts:
Hello,

I have a small dataset of Argos locations for 3 individuals over two summers. I have filtered out low-quality points. I have an average of 18 observations per individual, ranging from 4 to 43. My question is, do my samples have enough points to trust the HREs?

Thank you,
Vlad

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Minimum sample size
parts:
Hi Vlad,

If you turn on the location error model, then you shouldn't have any problems keeping the lower quality location estimates: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ctmm/vignettes/error.html

4 good quality location estimates is enough for home-range estimation, if they are not sampled too closely in time and if there is enough variance in the movement compared to the location error. You will find this out quickly when selecting an autocorrelation model and you get back the effective sample size for the area estimates, DOF[area] .

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 7f93d72765248a41
messages.subject: Re: Minimum sample size
parts:
Thanks, Chris. It does look like it should work as the sampling events are 4, 17, and 2 days apart, the error radii are <430 m, and the semi-variance in the variogram is no less than 0.65 square km.  DOF[area]  =  3. Please let me know if you don't agree. 

I did try some error models with all points, but those estimates seem highly improbable with home ranges nearing 4000 square km. 

Best,
Vlad

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Minimum sample size
parts:
Hi Vlad,

The data sound to be acceptable, but the results with all points sounds unusual and with an error model it's unlikely that the DOF comes out to be an integer even with only good points.
  1. Are the Argos error ellipses being imported by as.telemetry()? This should happen if the data are in Movebank format. When you run head() on an individual telemetry object, you should see error ellipse columns: COV.x.x, COV.x.y, COV.y.y
  2. Are you turning on the error model in the guess object, like in the vignette?
Best,
Chris
